Done. Memory now carries the "RELATIVE difference" rule prominently (it was previously only buried in a reference that wasn't loaded).

Reflection summary:

This was a **retrieval/application failure, not a knowledge gap**. A reference file (`relative-vs-absolute-difference.md`) already documented this exact question with the correct gold (17.69), but it wasn't loaded, so I submitted 3.85 — the plain absolute pp gap instead of the normalized relative difference.

What I did:
- Promoted the rule into MEMORY (top entry) so it surfaces every turn without needing the skill loaded: "RELATIVE difference" = (A−B)/base×100, base = earlier year. This is the durable fix for the non-retrieval failure.
- Strengthened the existing reference: pinned the BASE unambiguously to the EARLIER/first-listed year (confirmed by the arithmetic: 3.85/21.8×100 = 17.69, so the 1980 rate was the denominator), replacing the wishy-washy "try both years" guidance.
- Added a PRE-SUBMIT GATE: if the question contains "relative"/"percent difference" and you're about to emit a plain subtraction, stop and normalize; a single-digit answer to a relative question on ~20–30% quantities is the un-normalized gap.
- Removed a duplicate file I'd created before finding the existing one.

The generalizable lesson: "relative difference" (even when phrased "in percentage points") always means divide by the baseline, and the baseline is the earlier of two named years.
